title: colapsar mensagens longas com marcador de linhas escondidas
description: Uma mensagem de agente de ~2 mil caracteres come a tela inteira e enterra o resto do canal. Limitar a N linhas na timeline com marcador explicito ('… +37 linhas') e expandir apenas a mensagem selecionada. Unico item da trilha visual que nao e enfeite (GOAL 2026-08-22, secao 12, item 1). Altura de linha variavel: a timeline do chat nao esta sob o contrato de lockstep do sidebar, mas a mudanca de altura reflui o painel — chamar AppState::request_full_repaint() na expansao/colapso, senao o encoder de diff desincroniza o terminal (AGENTS.md, regra binding de 2026-08-13).
acceptance_criteria: Mensagem de 2k caracteres renderiza em N linhas mais marcador com a contagem real de linhas escondidas. Expandir a selecionada mostra o texto inteiro e forca repaint completo. Teste que fica VERMELHO se o clamp sair — um teste que passa sem o clamp e vacuo.
close_reason: entregue e verificado pelo lead; ver GATES.md

title: P1 · filtrar o remetente do conjunto de broadcast
description:
channel_agent_member_pane_ids (src/app/api/channels.rs:1296-1302) monta o conjunto de broadcast com todos os panes-agente membros, sem filtrar o autor. Resultado medido no #bun-nix: deliveries [w22:p6 deferred, w4Y:p2 deferred] com w22:p6 sendo o próprio remetente, que acumula 6 não-lidas das mensagens que ele mesmo escreveu.

O filtro vive em channel_agent_member_pane_ids e em nenhum chamador — contrato do épico. Barra externa: orc faz o mesmo com grep -vxF "$nick" (bin/orc:722,732); mesma topologia de canal deve produzir a mesma lista de destinatários.

Corolário registrado no GOAL §4: o eco é exclusivo do broadcast; --to <nick> já entrega limpo hoje.

title: transporte de bora channel: eco, seq, protocolo, persistência (escopo B′)
description:
Os quatro furos de TRANSPORTE do canal, escopo B′ decidido pelo Ary em 2026-08-22. Plano completo, com a perícia que o fundamenta: .local/prd/GOAL-2026-08-22.md no checkout MAIN ~/Sites/bora (.local é untracked — worktrees não têm; ler do main).

Fronteira que este épico respeita (CANAL-ESCOPO.md): bora é transporte e store, orc é UX e política. Os quatro furos são todos de transporte.

Contrato entre peças, fixado para rodarem sem negociação: nenhuma peça altera a assinatura de channel.send; o filtro de remetente vive em channel_agent_member_pane_ids e em nenhum chamador; o seq entra no texto injetado como prefixo [#canal seq=N from <pane> <nick>], mantendo os campos existentes na ordem atual.

Cortadas de propósito, ver GOAL §11: `bora channel say` (from_human é âncora de confiança com #[serde(skip)] — um cliente de socket não pode reivindicar o assento humano, e a peça original destruiria o modelo que pretendia completar) e o amortecedor de surto (já portado do orc: ui.channel_burst_messages=8 / ui.channel_burst_window_secs=600).

Barra a bater: bin/orc do ~/Sites/orchestrator, snapshot `git -C ~/Sites/orchestrator show HEAD:bin/orc`.
Regras do repo: ler a cadeia de AGENTS.md antes. Commits conventional minúsculos com refs #. Builders nunca rodam just check/test — o lead do épico roda os gates uma vez por fase.
acceptance_criteria: Broadcast não ecoa no remetente; o seq é legível de dentro do agente e alimenta tail --after; uma mensagem enfileirada sobrevive a restart do servidor; o CHANNEL_PROTOCOL define o namespace de nick e anuncia o assento humano. just check verde.
close_reason: escopo B' completo: .1 .2 .3 .4 fechados e verdes em main

title: project store: projects.yml, watcher, socket verbs, MCP writers
description:
Foundation for the Project view. A project is user-declared: name, channel, members (directories), sections, orchestrator. Single store, many writers, ONE reader (the sidebar reads the file + watch; never writes).

- Schema (design section 'Composition model'): defaults{open_with, checks, commands} + projects.<slug>{name, channel, members[{dir, worktrees: all|this}], orchestrator{agent, member, run_file}, sections{checks: [providers], commands: [names]}}. Member identity is a DIRECTORY; repo/checkout/subdir derived via existing git discovery (path -> GitSpaceMetadata, src/workspace/git/discovery.rs:4-14). repo: does not exist in the schema.
- Store at ~/.config/bora/projects.yml; serde_yaml or equivalent; parse errors -> toast + keep last good, never panic.
- Socket verbs project.list/create/update/member_add/member_remove via the 5-step Method pattern: (1) Method variant + params src/api/schema.rs:44-277 + new src/api/schema/projects.rs; (2) api_method_name arm src/api/server.rs:411-503; (3) catch-all dispatch_to_app handles plain verbs; (4) app-side match src/app/api.rs:1035-1356 -> handle_* in src/app/api/projects.rs; (5) responses::encode_success/error.
- MCP: one ALLOWLIST line each in src/mcp/tools.rs:20-32 — this is what lets an orchestrator assemble its own project at runtime.

title: windows: scripts/windows_check.ps1 clippy targeted --bin herdr, which does not exist
description: Found and fixed in passing while adding the production-only unwrap gate; filing for the record because it is the fork-merge-friction class AGENTS.md documents under 'renamed paths in tooling, not just strings'. scripts/windows_check.ps1 invoked cargo clippy --bin herdr. This fork's only bin target is bora (Cargo.toml name = bora, no explicit [[bin]]; cargo metadata confirms ['bora']), so just check and just lint on Windows would have failed with 'no bin target named herdr' - a failure that only appears on the Windows leg, never in a macOS or Linux run. Fixed to --bin bora in the same change that added the unwrap gate. Note the distinction that makes this easy to get wrong: the Windows install ecosystem deliberately keeps herdr.exe as the shipped filename, but --bin names the CARGO TARGET, which follows the package name.

title: projects: honor WorktreesScope::All in the Project-view matcher
description: Member.worktrees: WorktreesScope defaults to All (src/persist/projects.rs:178, :233-236; the doc example at :538 reads "repo derived; worktrees: all (default)"), and the API exposes it (ProjectMemberInfo.worktrees). The render-path matcher never reads it: workspace_matches_member (src/ui/sidebar/project_view.rs:144-156) requires space.checkout_key == member.checkout_key. checkout_key is canonicalize_best_effort_path(repo_root) (src/workspace/git/discovery.rs:83) and a linked worktree repo_root is its own path -- verified live: git rev-parse --show-toplevel in ~/Sites/worktrees/bora/worktree-calm-river-2881 returns that worktree, not ~/Sites/oss-team/bora. So a workspace in a linked worktree of a declared member dir does not match the project and falls into the trailing Ungrouped row, which is the opposite of what worktrees: all promises and defeats the whole point of making worktree a real level (sidebar-design decision #1/#2). Discovered while scoping bora-qdi, which it blocks: attaching unopened worktrees to a project by repo identity while the matcher stays on exact-checkout equality would make a dimmed row jump to Ungrouped the moment the user opened it.
acceptance_criteria: ResolvedMember carries the scope. workspace_matches_member honors it: This keeps exact repo_identity+checkout_key equality; All matches on repo_identity only, keeping subdir containment. A test proves a workspace whose checkout_key differs but whose repo_identity matches lands under the project under All and under Ungrouped under This. Matcher still does zero disk I/O (render path).
close_reason: ResolvedMember carries the declaring Member's scope, attached in ProjectsStore::resolve_all (the one site holding both the fresh MemberResolution and the Member) rather than widening resolve_member(dir: &str). workspace_matches_member honors it: This keeps repo_identity+checkout_key equality, All matches repo_identity only and keeps the subdir containment (which generalizes correctly because ws_subdir is already relative to the workspace's own repo_root). Still zero disk I/O on the render path. Test worktrees_scope_all_matches_other_checkouts_this_requires_exact_checkout; mutation M-scope (drop the This condition) reddens it. Was the blocking prerequisite for bora-qdi.

title: lint: AGENTS.md forbids unwrap() in production but nothing enforces it
description: AGENTS.md Code Conventions says "Rust: no unwrap() in production code." Cargo.toml [lints.clippy] (lines 24-45) configures redundant_clone, cloned_instead_of_copied, implicit_clone, cast_lossless, redundant_closure_for_method_calls as deny and dbg_macro, todo, cognitive_complexity, too_many_lines as warn -- clippy::unwrap_used appears nowhere in the repo (grep -rn unwrap_used over *.toml and *.rs returns nothing), and just lint passes only -D warnings plus four -A allows. So the rule is stated and unenforced: a production unwrap() lands green through just check and CI. Found while auditing a change under the unlazy gate discipline: the gate had to hand-scope its own check (added lines with unwrap() below each file`s cfg(test) boundary) precisely because clippy could not answer the question. Per the DOX guidance in AGENTS.md ("machine-checkable rules -> a script wired into the gate"), a rule this cheap to check should not depend on reviewer attention.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) clippy::unwrap_used = "deny" in [lints.clippy] with expect/allow annotations on the existing production violations, each carrying the justification comment AGENTS.md already requires for #[allow], and just check green; or (b) the rule is explicitly downgraded in AGENTS.md to advisory with the reason, so no one else mistakes it for enforced. Whichever is chosen, a count of current production violations is reported first -- the decision depends on whether it is 3 or 300.
close_reason: 48 -> 0 production clippy::unwrap_used, and the rule is now machine-enforced. Enforcement lives in the justfile, NOT Cargo.toml [lints.clippy]: that table has no per-target scope, so deny there also hit the hundreds of legitimate unwraps in test fixtures and turned just check red. just lint now runs clippy twice - --all-targets with -A clippy::unwrap_used, then --bins with -D clippy::unwrap_used, which is exactly the production scope AGENTS.md names because --bins does not compile cfg(test) modules. Mirrored in scripts/windows_check.ps1. Proven non-blind: injecting one production unwrap() fails the build with 'error: used unwrap() on an Option value'. Zero bare #[allow]: 39 Class-1 serialization sites collapsed onto three single-owner encode helpers (6 deleted outright as literal duplicates of print_response's error branch), 9 Class-2 invariant lookups got expect() naming what guarantees the value. The builder corrected my own bead: the split is 39/9, not the 42/6 the description claimed.
